identity.name: Vingt-8 ISO
identity.one_liner: The Vingt-8 ISO keeps Voutilainen's calibre 28 but changes how the dial is read: the hour hand turns once every twelve hours while the minute hand turns thirteen times an hour, so the time comes from the two hands' relation to each other, not from a glance.

comps.condition: Phillips New York Watch Auction: XIV (sale held 13-14 June 2026), lot 140. Circa 2017, 18k white gold, movement no. 28ISO-2, in-house cal. 28 with 35 jewels, 39mm. Phillips: likely the 2nd Vingt-8 ISO ever made and the 2nd sold by Phillips. Sold for USD 1,206,500 as published by Phillips; estimate USD 100,000-200,000. Accompanied by certificate booklet dated February 2017, warranty/service booklet, additional crocodile strap, box guarantee and fitted Vichard presentation box.

provenance_events.description: Phillips dates lot 140 to circa 2017 and records that the ISO's rotating display required a newly configured movement, slightly thicker than the standard Caliber 28.

The Phillips lot offered in New York in June 2026 carries a Voutilainen certificate booklet dated February 2017 and movement number 28ISO-2, which Phillips reads as likely the second ISO Voutilainen built.

provenance_events.person_or_event: Phillips New York Watch Auction: XIV, lot 140
provenance_events.description: The Vingt-8 ISO offered as lot 140 sold for USD 1,206,500 against an estimate of USD 100,000-200,000, about six times the high estimate. The sale was held 13-14 June 2026; Phillips calls this likely the 2nd Vingt-8 ISO ever made and the 2nd sold by the house.

narrative.story:
The Vingt-8 ISO changes what a dial asks of you. Phillips says its display takes inspiration from the psychologist Daniel Kahneman's account of two ways the brain forms thoughts: System 1, fast and intuitive, and System 2, slow and deliberate. Reading a regular watch is System 1. The ISO is built to make the wearer engage with time differently. The hour hand turns at the normal 12-hour speed while the minute hand turns 13 times every hour. At the full hour the two hands overlap; at every half hour they sit exactly opposite; at the quarter hours they are 90 degrees apart. The time is read from the hands in relation to each other, not against the minute scale on the outer ring.

The movement is Voutilainen's own. Phillips describes the Caliber 28 as using two escape wheels that deliver direct impulses to a sizeable balance wheel, reducing friction compared with a traditional Swiss lever escapement. European Watch describes a free-sprung balance with a Breguet overcoil and a Grossman spiral. The rotating display needed a newly configured movement, slightly thicker than the standard Caliber 28; the watch Phillips sold carries 35 jewels.

The sale is the evidence about how rare it is. Phillips calls lot 140 likely the 2nd Vingt-8 ISO ever made, judging from its movement number, 28ISO-2, and only the 2nd sold by Phillips. It carried an estimate of USD 100,000 to 200,000 and sold for USD 1,206,500. Phillips also says the St-Sulpice manufacture still produces fewer than 60 pieces per year.
narrative.collector_notes: No retail price is on file for the ISO, so this register carries an empty MSRP history rather than a borrowed one. The only sale on file is the Phillips New York lot, one data point, so no market value is computed. Scarcity here rests on the brand-level production figure alone (fewer than 60 pieces a year, per Phillips); the register has no evidence that the ISO is a numbered or limited edition.
